question_text: Why can it be dangerous if you, as the last in a queue, immediately overtake as soon as the oncoming traffic is past?

options.text: Because you must reckon with others in the queue swinging out to overtake
Because the distance needed to overtake might not be sufficient
Because if you perhaps need to push back into the queue, this could lead to an accident

correct_answers.text: Because you must reckon with others in the queue swinging out to overtake
Because the distance needed to overtake might not be sufficient
Because if you perhaps need to push back into the queue, this could lead to an accident

comment: If a convoy has formed, drivers should basically overtake one after the other. The last of a convoy has the longest overtaking path and must also expect other vehicles starting to overtake in front of him.

question_text: What must you remember if you want to overtake?

options.text: The van could start to overtake the vehicle travelling in front of it
Oncoming traffic could appear
As no oncoming traffic is in sight, you may overtake without hesitation

correct_answers.text: The van could start to overtake the vehicle travelling in front of it
Oncoming traffic could appear

comment: In an overtaking maneuver you should make sure that the oncoming lane is free. Be sure that there are no bends or gates as well and you only overtake a car. Watch out for more road users, especially trucks.

question_text: Are you allowed to overtake the black car on this autobahn on the right?

options.text: No, because there is no queue of vehicles in the left lane
Yes, if you do not drive faster than 80 km/h
Yes, because there is enough space to overtake

correct_answers.text: No, because there is no queue of vehicles in the left lane

comment: The black car may not be overtaken on the right in this example. On freeways and highways, you may only overtake on the right as an exception. This is the case, for example, when a vehicle queue has formed on the left.

question_text:
Both cars are travelling at about 30 km/h. Are you allowed to overtake both before the bend?
No, because

options.text: - the distance you need to overtake would be too great
- the light-coloured car could pull out to overtake
- you are not allowed to cross the broken line

correct_answers.text: - the distance you need to overtake would be too great
- the light-coloured car could pull out to overtake

comment: You may go over the broken line. An overtaking process would still be too dangerous here, because the manageable distance to overtake before the turn is too short. You also have to expect that the driver of the light car will start to overtake.

question_text: The driver of the overtaking car has evidently made a miscalculation. What must you do?

options.text: Brake immediately and veer to the right
Proceed as before

correct_answers.text: Brake immediately and veer to the right

comment: The car driver should reduce the speed. Otherwise an accident could occur. If this is not enough, you could additionally fall back on the grass verge on the right.

question_text: You want to overtake. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I refrain from overtaking
I accelerate
I maintain my speed

correct_answers.text: I refrain from overtaking

comment: As the vehicle behind you has already started the overtaking process, you should refrain from overtaking.

question_text:
You want to overtake. What should you do?
I overtake

options.text: - only if I have a clear view over the necessary stretch of road
- only if there is no oncoming vehicle
- at the same time, as the [blue car]

correct_answers.text: - only if I have a clear view over the necessary stretch of road
- only if there is no oncoming vehicle

comment: Here you can overtake if you can see over the required distance and if there is no oncoming vehicle (limited visibility).

question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake here?

options.text: Because the visible stretch is not sufficient
Because I would not be able to maintain an adequate distance to the side in the event of oncoming traffic
Because I am not permitted to cross the central line

correct_answers.text: Because the visible stretch is not sufficient
Because I would not be able to maintain an adequate distance to the side in the event of oncoming traffic

comment: In general, you must not overtake if the entire overtaking distance is not visible or the side clearance to other road users cannot be met. Both negative factors are given in the present situation: The assessable track is too short for a safe overtaking maneuver. The minimum distance to the cyclists of 1.5 m cannot be met with oncoming traffic.

question_text:
You are being overtaken and the oncoming traffic is getting dangerously close. Despite this the other vehicle continues with the overtaking manoeuvre. What should you do?
I drive as far to the right-side as possible and

options.text: - reduce my speed
- maintain my speed
- increase my speed

correct_answers.text: - reduce my speed

comment: You have to slow down and drive to the right, so that the overtaking vehicle driver can go back into lane on time. In no case should you increase the speed if you are overtaken.

question_text: Why should you brake hard now?

options.text: Because of the car
Because of the truck
Because of the tractor

correct_answers.text: Because of the car

comment: Since the blue passenger car will most likely get on your lane, you have to slow down immediately and keep to the right.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: I overtake [the blue car] and then move into the middle lane
I overtake [the red van] and then move into the middle lane
I brake slightly to prompt the vehicle behind to keep its distance

correct_answers.text: I overtake [the blue car] and then move into the middle lane

comment: As the car driver, you do not have to dodge to the middle lane when another car pushes you from behind or uses the flash light. You should overtake the blue car and the red van as usual. To change safely to the middle lane, the overtaking process must be completed. Only then you can change.

question_text: You want to overtake. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I cease the overtaking manoeuvre and remain behind the truck
I accelerate and quickly continue the overtaking manoeuvre
I maintain my speed and continue the overtaking manoeuvre

correct_answers.text: I cease the overtaking manoeuvre and remain behind the truck

comment: You already indicated and want to overtake the truck. In the rearview mirror you can see a red car approaching on the left lane at high speed. You need to stop the overtaking process immediately and stay behind the truck. If you continue, you force the red car to brake suddenly. He could drive against your car.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: I quickly continue the overtaking manoeuvre
I cease the overtaking manoeuvre, and pull back into the right-hand lane
I brake, but continue the overtaking manoeuvre

correct_answers.text: I quickly continue the overtaking manoeuvre

comment: While overtaking a truck, you observe a fast approaching car in the rearview mirror. It is too late to complete the overtaking process. Accelerate and complete the overtaking process quickly but safely. Basically, subsequent vehicles do not have priority; even not on the freeway.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: I overtake the van and then move into the middle lane
I move immediately into the lane to the right
I brake slightly to prompt the vehicle behind to keep its distance

correct_answers.text: I overtake the van and then move into the middle lane

comment: A driver drives dangerously close to you on the left-hand lane and signals his/her overtaking intent with his flash light. You should still overtake the transporter on the mid-lane and then get back into the lane in front of it to defuse the situation.

question_text: Why must you slow down here?

options.text: Because of the overtaking car
Because the maximum permitted speed is 80 km/h
Because of the tractor

correct_answers.text: Because of the overtaking car

comment: The oncoming car overtakes despite opposing traffic about 250 m in front of you. You have to reduce your speed and drive to the far right. So, you defuse the situation and give the overtaking car more time and space to complete the overtaking process. The tractor moves away from the intersection and poses no danger.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I slow down
I drive as far to the right-side as possible
I accelerate

correct_answers.text: I slow down
I drive as far to the right-side as possible

comment: If a car overtakes you despite oncoming traffic, you should delay and try to drive to the right as far as possible. This gives the other vehicle enough space to safely complete the overtaking process.

question_text: You want to overtake. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I refrain from overtaking the truck, because I do not have a clear view over the necessary stretch of road
I follow the motorbike, because the truck is using its indicators to signal an opportunity to overtake
I reduce my distance to the truck, to enable me to overtake more quickly

correct_answers.text: I refrain from overtaking the truck, because I do not have a clear view over the necessary stretch of road

comment: You should not overtake the truck, as you cannot see the distance required for this.

question_text: Why must you abort your overtaking manoeuvre?

options.text: Because the tractor wants to turn left
Because it could obstruct oncoming traffic
Because a no-overtaking zone is visible ahead

correct_answers.text: Because the tractor wants to turn left
Because it could obstruct oncoming traffic

comment: You should abort the overtaking maneuver because the tractor wants to turn left and because oncoming traffic may be obstructed.

question_text:
What is the right course of action now?
I

options.text: - do not overtake, because the tractor wants to pull out to the left
- overtake carefully, because the tractor is demanding I do so
- overtake immediately, because the overtaking distance is large enough

correct_answers.text: - do not overtake, because the tractor wants to pull out to the left

comment: You should not overtake because the tractor will swerve to the left (see indicator).

question_text: You want to overtake. What is the right course of action here?

options.text: I do not overtake, because the [yellow] vehicle might want to overtake
I do not overtake, because oncoming traffic could emerge
I overtake, because no oncoming traffic is visible

correct_answers.text: I do not overtake, because the [yellow] vehicle might want to overtake
I do not overtake, because oncoming traffic could emerge

comment: The correct behavior (proactive) here is not to overtake as the yellow vehicle could overtake and oncoming traffic could appear (restricted view).

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I brake immediately
I drive as far to the right as possible
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I brake immediately
I drive as far to the right as possible

comment: As a vehicle is in your lane, you should slow down immediately and as far as possible turn right to avoid a collision.

question_text:
Why are you not allowed to overtake now?
Because of the

options.text: - motorbike
- layout of the road
- [red] car

correct_answers.text: - motorbike
- layout of the road

comment: Because of the motorcycle (oncoming traffic) and the course of the road and the resulting poor visibility, you are not allowed to overtake the cyclist.

question_text:
Why are you not allowed to overtake here now?
Because of the

options.text: - motorbike
- [red car]
- signposted prohibition on overtaking

correct_answers.text: - motorbike

comment: At this moment, a motorcyclist passes the tractor. Wait until you can safely begin the overtaking manoeuvre.

question_text:
Why are you not allowed to overtake here?
Because I

options.text: - do not have an adequate view of the road ahead
- cannot maintain an adequate passing distance from the cyclists if there is any oncoming traffic
- may not cross over the central lane markings

correct_answers.text: - do not have an adequate view of the road ahead
- cannot maintain an adequate passing distance from the cyclists if there is any oncoming traffic

comment: Due to the curve and the trees, you cannot see the rest of the road sufficiently. Out of town, you must keep a minimum distance of 2 metres to the side of cyclists. In the event of sudden oncoming traffic, you would not be able to maintain this distance when overtaking. Therefore, you must not overtake here.

question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake here?

options.text: Because the side clearance to the cyclists is too small
Because I may endanger oncoming traffic
Because I may not cross the centre line

correct_answers.text: Because the side clearance to the cyclists is too small
Because I may endanger oncoming traffic

comment: The road is too small to allow enough side distance to cyclists and oncoming traffic at the same time.

question_text: You want to overtake on a tree-lined avenue. What special aspect should you bear in mind?

options.text: Side clearances are frequently misjudged in this situation
Vehicles with high superstructures frequently perform evasive manoeuvres to avoid branches in this situation
Accidents involving trees are particularly frequent here

correct_answers.text: Side clearances are frequently misjudged in this situation
Vehicles with high superstructures frequently perform evasive manoeuvres to avoid branches in this situation
Accidents involving trees are particularly frequent here

comment: The avenue is framed by trees. Therefore, the change of light and shadow often leads to the incorrect estimation of distances. Likewise, it can often lead to trees falling and vehicles with high bodies trying to avoid branches.

question_text: Why must you discontinue your overtaking manoeuvre here?

options.text: Because the tractor will turn off to the left
Because the motorbike will overtake me
Because I can see a no-overtaking sign

correct_answers.text: Because the tractor will turn off to the left

comment: The tractor starts to turn left. The tractor drives across the left lane of the road. If you overtake now, you would collide with the tractor.

question_text: You are driving on a road with one lane for each direction. A convoy of motor vehicles is driving up ahead of you. Why should you refrain from overtaking in order to prevent a dangerous situation from occurring?

options.text: Because the overtaking distance is considerably larger than with single vehicles
Because I should not break the convoy by pulling back into my lane early
Because I cannot assess the road traffic situation ahead of the convoy

correct_answers.text: Because the overtaking distance is considerably larger than with single vehicles
Because I should not break the convoy by pulling back into my lane early
Because I cannot assess the road traffic situation ahead of the convoy

comment:
A group of pedestrians, cyclists or motor vehicles, which is traveling together in road traffic, is called a closed association. Closed associations must be clearly marked and must not be interrupted.
Because a closed association consists of several vehicles, you cannot really understand the traffic situation. When overtaking a closed bandage, you should avoid premature inserting, which makes the overtaking path significantly longer.

question_text: Why is it dangerous to overtake in this situation?

options.text: Because vehicles ahead may swerve out
Because I cannot see far enough along the route necessary for overtaking
Because there is not sufficient space to pull back in between the vehicles ahead

correct_answers.text: Because vehicles ahead may swerve out
Because I cannot see far enough along the route necessary for overtaking
Because there is not sufficient space to pull back in between the vehicles ahead

comment:
You are driving in a convoy of several cars behind a lorry on a winding road with oncoming traffic. Ideally, the car behind the lorry overtakes first before the vehicles behind move up and start to overtake. 
On the left-hand bend, you cannot see the overtaking lane sufficiently. You will probably have to cancel the overtaking manoeuvre and pull in between two vehicles. There is a possibility that the distance between the vehicles in front is too small and that you will endanger yourself and other road users by pulling in.

question_text: The vehicles ahead of you are driving at about 30 km/h. Why are you not permitted to overtake before the road bend?

options.text: Because my overtaking distance is too long
Because the [red] car might pull out to overtake
Because I am not permitted to cross the lane marking

correct_answers.text: Because my overtaking distance is too long
Because the [red] car might pull out to overtake

comment: You are not allowed to overtake before the bend as your overtaking distance is too long to overtake both vehicles before the bend. There is also not enough distance between the two cars for you to pull in. In addition, the red car has the right of way to overtake in front of you; if you both start the overtaking manoeuvre, there is a danger for you and oncoming traffic. As the bend is not visible, you cannot know whether oncoming traffic is coming.

question_text:
Why do you have to switch to the right-hand lane?
Because of the

options.text: - [red] car
- [blue] car
- [yellow tractor]

correct_answers.text: - [red] car

comment:
The traffic sign indicates a narrowing (end of a lane) in 200 metres. 
The lane is led into oncoming traffic through the narrowing, so you must be extra vigilant not to end up in oncoming traffic.

options.text: I do not overtake the [cyclists] for now
I overtake the [cyclists]
I sound my horn to prompt the [cyclists] to ride one behind the other

correct_answers.text: I do not overtake the [cyclists] for now

comment: You should not overtake for the time being, as you are driving side by side and you can't keep enough lateral distance.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I slow down to walking speed
I drive over to the right-side as far as possible
I drive on past the pedestrian

correct_answers.text: I slow down to walking speed
I drive over to the right-side as far as possible

comment: In such a situation, you must slow down to walking speed and keep to the right as much as possible. You should not drive past the pedestrians because the danger is too high.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I maintain my speed
I overtake [the cyclist]

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed

comment: You have to reduce your speed because the side distance to the cyclist cannot be kept.

question_text: Why should you not overtake the moped rider in this situation?

options.text: Because this might cause the moped rider to fall
Because I am not allowed to drive significantly faster than the moped rider
Because I am unable to maintain the requisite amount of side clearance

correct_answers.text: Because this might cause the moped rider to fall
Because I am not allowed to drive significantly faster than the moped rider
Because I am unable to maintain the requisite amount of side clearance

comment:
In the roadworks area, the speed limit is 30 km/h and the road is narrowed. 
You are therefore not allowed to drive as fast as would be necessary to overtake the moped rider safely. 
Due to the narrowness of the road, you cannot keep the required distance to the side and the poor condition of the road could cause the moped rider to fall if you overtake him.
